# forgo: vet analyzes .fgo files, including their forgo syntax
# (postfix if, throw, and ?), instead of reporting no files.

go vet m/clean
! stderr .

! go vet m/bad
stderr 'bad\.fgo:6:\d+: fmt\.Printf format %d has arg s of wrong type string'

# go test runs vet on .fgo files too.
go test m/clean
stdout '^ok'

-- go.mod --
module m

go 1.27
-- clean/clean.fgo --
package clean

import (
	"errors"
	"strconv"
)

var errEmpty = errors.New("empty")

func F(s string) (n int, err error) {
	throw errEmpty if s == ""
	throw "too long" if len(s) > 100
	n = strconv.Atoi(s)?
	return
}
-- clean/clean_test.go --
package clean

import "testing"

func TestF(t *testing.T) {
	if n, err := F("12"); n != 12 || err != nil {
		t.Fatal(n, err)
	}
}
-- bad/bad.fgo --
package bad

import "fmt"

func F(s string) {
	fmt.Printf("%d\n", s) if s != ""
}
